# komodo_procedure (Resource)

Manages a Komodo procedure: an ordered list of stages, each running one or more executions (deploy a stack, run a build, pull a repo, ...) in parallel. A procedure can run on a schedule, from a webhook, or on demand.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Nightly: pull the config repo, then redeploy any stack whose files changed.
resource "komodo_procedure" "nightly_deploy" {
  name              = "nightly-deploy"
  schedule_format   = "Cron"
  schedule          = "0 0 2 * * ?" # seconds minutes hours day month weekday
  schedule_timezone = "America/New_York"
  schedule_alert    = false # only alert on failure

  stages = [
    {
      name = "Pull config"
      executions = [{
        type   = "PullRepo"
        params = jsonencode({ repo = komodo_repo.config.id })
      }]
    },
    {
      name = "Deploy changed stacks"
      # Executions in one stage run in parallel.
      executions = [
        {
          type   = "DeployStackIfChanged"
          params = jsonencode({ stack = komodo_stack.app.id })
        },
        {
          type   = "BatchDeployStackIfChanged"
          params = jsonencode({ pattern = "media-*" })
        },
      ]
    },
    {
      name    = "Prune"
      enabled = false # kept in config but skipped
      executions = [{
        type   = "PruneImages"
        params = jsonencode({ server = komodo_server.main.id })
      }]
    },
  ]

  tags = ["system"]
}

# Plain-English schedule; an execution without params.
resource "komodo_procedure" "backup" {
  name     = "backup-core-database"
  schedule = "every day at 1am"

  stages = [{
    name       = "Backup"
    executions = [{ type = "BackupCoreDatabase" }]
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description shown in the Komodo UI. Leave it out and Terraform does not manage it; set it to "" to clear it.
- `failure_alert` (Boolean) Send an alert when the procedure fails.
- `schedule` (String) When to run the procedure. Cron uses six fields with seconds first, for example "0 0 3 * * ?". Empty means no schedule.
- `schedule_alert` (Boolean) Send an alert each time the schedule runs.
- `schedule_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the schedule is active when one is set.
- `schedule_format` (String) How schedule is written: "English" (for example "every day at 3am") or "Cron".
- `schedule_timezone` (String) TZ identifier for the schedule, for example "America/New_York". Empty uses Komodo Core's timezone.
- `stages` (Attributes List) Stages, run one after another. The executions inside a stage run in parallel. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--stages))
- `tags` (List of String) List of tag names to apply to this procedure.
- `template` (Boolean) Mark the resource as a template in Komodo. Leave it out and Terraform does not manage the flag.
- `webhook_enabled` (Boolean) Whether incoming webhooks trigger the procedure.
- `webhook_secret` (String, Sensitive) Alternate webhook secret for this procedure. Empty uses the default secret from Komodo Core's config.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier.

<a id="nestedatt--stages"></a>
### Nested Schema for `stages`

Required:

- `executions` (Attributes List) Executions run in parallel within this stage. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--stages--executions))
- `name` (String) Stage name.

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the stage runs. A disabled stage is skipped.

<a id="nestedatt--stages--executions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `stages.executions`

Required:

- `type` (String) Execution type, for example DeployStack, BatchDeployStackIfChanged, Deploy, RunBuild, PullRepo, RunProcedure, RunAction, GlobalAutoUpdate, BackupCoreDatabase or Sleep. See the Komodo API reference for the full list.

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this execution runs.
- `params` (String) Parameters of the execution as a JSON object, for example jsonencode({ stack = komodo_stack.app.id }). Komodo fills in defaults and replaces resource names with IDs when it saves; those rewrites are not shown as changes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing procedure by its Komodo ID.
terraform import komodo_procedure.backup 65a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1
```
